score.note: First structural draft, not a permutation search. Read games/gs1/asm/080d41a4.s in full and cross-checked every pc-relative literal load against its resolved byte offset (script-computed, not guessed) to pin every constant, table address, and call target before writing any C. The family-matcher's assigned template (main:080ce85c, games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c, score 7938/10000) supplied the field-offset layout (work+0x7780/0x7784/0x7824/0x7828), the M2C_FIELD macro, the DrawRectangleFn typedef, and the heap_cache cursor-advance idiom, but the owner's actual body is a different sub-effect entirely: no scanline sine-curve, no 32x32 orbit sprites. Instead it runs a per-"kind" loop (0..count-1, count read from a byte table at 0x080ee25e indexed by state->0x18) that draws a growing-then-shrinking marker via two DrawRectangleFn-style blits, spawns particles into the shared 1024-entry 0x02010000 pool on the middle frame of each kind's window, and updates every party member's position once per kind; a second, unconditional pass ages and redraws every live particle in that same pool every frame. Confirmed the r4-slot `_call_via_rN` trampoline finding from games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json applies here too: what reads as `bl Func_080072f4` at three call sites is an indirect call through a DrawRectangleFn value already sitting in a register (rectangle[0], or rectangle_slot[scan&1] in the decay pass) -- modeled as `((DrawRectangleFn)ptr)(dest,src,x,y,w,h)`, not a call to a real function. The two `bl Func_080072f0` sites are the r3-slot trampoline instead, modeled per games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/battle/battle_owner_12.c's established direct-call-with-trailing-target convention (`Func_080072f0(a,b,c,target)`). Cross-checked every ROM table this owner reads (0x080ee25e, 0x080ee250, 0x080ee244) against games/gs1/assets/code/sentou_kouka_hyou_a.json's byte dump to confirm the count/sprite-index/spawn-count semantics before writing the loop bounds -- all three matched the derived formulas exactly (e.g. Data_080ee25e = [1,3,7,0], consistent with a 0..3 state kind and a per-kind loop count). Iterated against `compiler candidate-show --align --size 1096`: fixed the Func_080ed408/heap_cache[7] read-before-second-call ordering to match the template's exact evaluation order (candidate dh 497->496); added the established Value_XXXXXXXX literal-pool-load idiom for both Func_080e0524 id arguments (0xd1, 0x73) instead of plain immediates; converted the 1024-entry zero-init loop to a do-while with increment-before-store to match the reference's r8-then-store order; restructured the per-kind range dispatch (originally written as clean delta-based if/else-if) into the literal fall-through/goto shape the reference's five-label control flow actually has once traced instruction-by-instruction, which alone dropped wrong_instructions by ~30; de-hoisted the sprite-table lookup and speed+32 sub-expression back into fresh per-site reads (the family's documented anti-CSE-spill pattern) instead of caching them across sites, matching the reference's repeated re-reads. Ran out of time before closing the remaining gap, which is dominated by two things: (1) a persistent one-slot (4-byte) stack-frame oversize (sub sp,#56 vs reference's #52) whose exact source was not pinned down -- tried collapsing/renaming count and count*8 several ways (a single `count*7+48` expression, a named count8 local, count8 computed inline) and the named-count8 form scored best (496->476 dh) but never closed the gap; (2) pervasive independent-immediate-load scheduling differences (same instructions, different order) throughout the per-kind draw and particle-spawn/decay blocks that read as the family's documented 'register allocator schedules independent loads differently' residual rather than a semantic error -- confirmed by re-tracing several of these regions by hand against the resolved literal table and finding the operations match, only the emission order differs. Semantic summary: battle-presentation sub-effect on the 0x03001eec battle-work subsystem. Loads a palette conditionally (skipped when state->0x18==2), zeroes the life field of all 1024 slots in the shared particle pool at 0x02010000, then runs (count*7)+48 frames where count comes from a per-state-kind byte table. Each frame optionally nudges a camera-shake field (state->0x18==2 case, frames 0..63 only), then for each of `count` "kind" indices j: on frame j*8 fires a flash callback + full-screen fade blit; on frame j*8+1 draws a shrinking marker; on frames j*8+2..3 draws a second marker and, on exactly j*8+2, spawns up to a per-kind target count of fresh particles into the first free pool slots with randomized angle/speed and a per-kind sprite type; on frame j*8+4 nudges every active party member's on-screen marker and portrait rotation. Independently, every frame, the whole 1024-slot particle pool is aged (life-1, position integrated via Func_080e3908) and any particle past a fixed altitude threshold that is still on-screen is redrawn as a shrinking trail sprite selected from a size-indexed lookup table, alternating between the effect's two draw routines by pool-slot parity.

Known open residual, not source-shape-controllable within this pass's time budget: a one-slot stack-frame size mismatch (56 vs reference's 52 bytes) whose exact cause was not isolated, plus widespread independent-immediate-load scheduling-order differences that read as the same 'register allocator/scheduler makes a different but equally valid choice' class of residual already documented for this owner family (080dc1ec.json, 080e01e4.json) -- do not force register assignment or chase further without new evidence.
